items.stem: When salt fully dissolves in water and you cannot see it, what has happened to it?

options.text: Its tiny particles have spread out evenly through the water
options.rationale: Correct: the solute particles spread through the solvent; the salt is still there.
Dissolving does not destroy the solute.
The salt is still salt, just spread out in the water.

options.text: The salt floated away as a gas
options.rationale: The salt stays dissolved in the liquid, it does not become a gas.

items.explanation: Correct: the solute particles spread through the solvent; the salt is still there.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO methods could separate salt dissolved in water? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Letting the water evaporate to leave the salt behind
options.rationale: Correct: evaporation removes the water and leaves the salt.

options.text: Boiling off the water with an adult's help to collect the salt
options.rationale: Correct: heating evaporates the water, leaving the salt.
Filtering cannot separate a dissolved solute; it passes through the paper.
Salt is not magnetic, so a magnet will not separate it.

items.explanation: Correct: evaporation removes the water and leaves the salt.

items.stem: Which change would make sugar dissolve FASTER in a cup of water?

options.rationale: Correct: higher temperature and stirring both speed up dissolving.

options.text: Using ice-cold water and not stirring
options.rationale: Cold, still water dissolves sugar more slowly.
Adding more sugar does not make a given amount dissolve faster.

options.text: Covering the cup with a lid
options.rationale: A lid does not speed up dissolving.

items.explanation: Correct: higher temperature and stirring both speed up dissolving.
